preamble: Affrication of the palatal stop [c] to the postalveolar affricate [tʃ] adds a fricated release and moves the closure slightly forward. It is the usual second step in velar palatalization chains (k > c > tʃ), but it can also be observed directly where a palatal stop phoneme exists: Albanian q /c/ merges with ç /tʃ/ for many speakers, and Macedonian ќ /c/ has merged with /tʃ/ in the urban Prilep subdialect.

examples.note: Some speakers merge the palatal stops q, gj into the palatoalveolar affricates ç, xh; the merger is especially common in Northern Gheg and increasingly found in Tosk.
In the urban Prilep subdialect of the Prilep-Bitola dialect, ќ and ѓ have merged into /tʃ/ and /dʒ/; northern dialects have alveolo-palatal [tɕ dʑ] instead.
